3.translation:
The three displayed rows refer to two biological sequences. ⟦shared:0⟧ values
identify sources; names identify instances. Filter each layer's original HSPs
before routing. ⟦shared:1⟧ accepts two names or two declaration-order indices.
Ambiguous routes fail. The two subsets below are disjoint and preserve every HSP.

6.translation:
The same ⟦shared:0⟧ can use ⟦shared:1⟧ or ⟦shared:2⟧.
Vertical Collinear changes the global view while keeping source strands and
positions. Positive local normal points left. Explicit text styles retain
priority. ⟦shared:3⟧ accepts an instance name; its inverse input
is final y in vertical views.

7.translation:
⟦shared:0⟧ supplies ⟦shared:1⟧, ⟦shared:2⟧ and
⟦shared:3⟧. Explicit ⟦shared:4⟧ detects repeated display across
layers; use ⟦shared:5⟧ only when that repetition is intended. Without
an ID, identity stays layer-local; equal row values do not establish identity.
